paragraphs.source_en: “On the twenty-first, Tanaka Denzayemon Nagayoshi, a retainer of the Hyōbu, captured the fugitive Ishida Mitsunari at Furuhashi in Ika District, Ōmi, and took him to the camp at Iguchi in the same district. Because Ishida ate a large quantity of raw rice while fleeing, he is suffering severe diarrhea and can scarcely walk; it will therefore be another day or two before he can be escorted to Your Lordship. It will likely be around the twenty-fifth.”

paragraphs.source_zh: “二十一日，兵部属下田中传左卫门长吉，在近江伊香郡古桥将逃亡中的石田三成一举抓获，并将其带至该郡井口阵中。由于石田在逃亡中吞食了大量生米，腹泻严重，举步维艰，故一两日之后方可押送到大人处。时间约为二十五日前后。”

paragraphs.source_en: When Honda Kōzuke-no-suke Masazumi relayed the report from Tanaka Hyōbu-tayū Yoshimasa to Ieyasu, Ieyasu instructed him, “Once he arrives, handle everything according to established custom.” He then ordered Ikeda Nagayoshi and Kamei Korenori jointly to deal with Natsuka Masaie and his son, who had fled from Mount Nangū to their castle at Minakuchi.

paragraphs.source_en: By then, Konishi Yukinaga and Ekei had also been captured separately and confined in a turret. Like Mitsunari, Konishi Yukinaga had escaped to Mount Ibuki, but, knowing there was no possibility of further flight, he surrendered voluntarily to the headman of Kasukabe Village at the mountain’s eastern foot. On receiving the headman’s report, a senior retainer of Takenaka Tango-no-kami Shigekado took Yukinaga into custody and brought him to Kusatsu, where he was subsequently handed over to Murakoshi Mosuke.

paragraphs.source_en: Amid such talk, at the hour of the Snake on the twenty-fifth day of the ninth month in the fifth year of Keichō, Mitsunari’s prisoner cage was escorted into Ōtsu under the guard of Tanaka Hyōbu-tayū. The instant they heard that Mitsunari had arrived, officers and soldiers crowded before the main camp to stare at him. It was hardly surprising, for every man under Ieyasu’s command hated Mitsunari to the marrow.
